traceability.notes: Story 010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS is fully implemented. The valid-annotation-format rule exposes both nested (story.pattern/req.pattern) and flat (storyPathPattern/requirementIdPattern) configuration options, compiles them into regexes with robust validation and error reporting, and falls back to previous hardcoded defaults when options are absent or invalid. Custom example strings for both story paths and requirement IDs are supported and correctly reflected in error messages, with nested configuration taking precedence over flat shorthand. A JSON schema is provided for ESLint to validate configuration options, and the defaults are aligned with the valid-story-reference rule’s expected story file layout so the two rules work together without conflict. Comprehensive Jest tests explicitly tied to this story verify custom patterns, fallback behavior, example message substitution, and precedence rules, and all those tests currently pass. Documentation in docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md clearly describes and exemplifies both nested and flat custom pattern configurations. Based on code, tests, and documentation, all acceptance criteria and listed requirements for this story are satisfied.
